steps.label: A classical bit is 0 or 1 — full stop
steps.sub: No in-between, no way to combine the two

steps.label: A qubit lives in a 2-dimensional complex vector space
General state: |ψ⟩ = a|0⟩ + b|1⟩
steps.sub: a and b are complex numbers called amplitudes

steps.label: One vector with components along both basis states
steps.sub: Not a choice between them — a different kind of object entirely

steps.label: a and b are NOT just probabilities
steps.sub: "60% chance of 0" is the wrong mental model

steps.label: Actual probabilities come later, via the Born rule
Complex numbers carry a phase; plain probabilities don't
steps.sub: Phase is what lets amplitudes interfere — add or cancel

steps.label: Interference is the mechanism algorithms exploit
steps.sub: A qubit isn't 'a bit with some hidden randomness'

caption: Amplitudes aren't free to be anything — they're locked together by the normalization constraint.
